parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of soldiers
a key is the solution to a puzzle, as in an answer key

explanation.surface: Troops confronting a crucial choice before battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' links the pieces, RE coming first. 'key' looks like an adjective (crucial) but works as a noun: the set of answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm resolve or formal ruling reached by a meeting is a decision.

clue.text: Residence occupied by one swimmer, flat

parts.note: a place is somewhere one lives, a residence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lone swimmer living in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' reads as a home beside 'Residence', but it describes the fish: a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The plaice is a flatfish, a swimmer that lies flat on the seabed.

clue.text: Being wrong about elite force getting hit-man

parts.note: as can mean being, as in 'as it was raining'
a sin is a wrong
the SAS is the British Army's elite Special Air Service

explanation.surface: Someone at fault over a special forces unit landing a contract killer.
explanation.walkthrough: AS and SIN are written round SAS. 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-man is a paid killer, a murderer for hire.

parts.note: not quick thinking but a presence in the sense of a being without a body, a ghost made of mind alone

explanation.surface: A question about keeping a cool head.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or soul is a non-bodily presence, a thing of the mind or soul rather than flesh.

indicators.note: basking means lolling about in the sun, so the letters sprawl into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian printmaker enjoying acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basking' rearranges IN PRAISE. Giovanni Battista Piranesi made famous etchings of Rome and imaginary prisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Piranesi was an eighteenth-century Italian artist known for his engraved views of Rome.

indicators.note: away tells us to send something off, so one letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a shred is a fragment

explanation.surface: Discard a scrap immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once', but 'right' gives R and 'away' removes it from SHRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to let fall or cast off, as a tree drops its leaves.

clue.text: Lift front off to see bird

indicators.note: front off says the leading letter is cut away from the word

parts.note: to lift something is to steal it

explanation.surface: Raise the front of something so you can spot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' reads as raise but means steal; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

parts.note: not a lively pop group but a long band that glows when the switch is flipped

explanation.surface: A question about a trendy group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluorescent tube is a long band of light that is switched on to light a room.

clue.text: Sip tea for ages after stirring cultural event

indicators.note: stirring mixes things round, as in a cup of tea, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone lingers over a cup of tea after giving it a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after stirring' puts the indicator after the fodder; 'after' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony marking a stage of life, such as coming of age, is an event in a culture.

clue.text: Leading party worker taking little time

parts.note: a do is a party
min is the short form of minute, a little time
the ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A senior party activist sparing only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' sits beside 'party' as if describing it; it is the definition. 'taking' links: the worker takes MIN before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dominant is in command or foremost, ahead of the rest.

clue.text: Foreign currency accepted outside West African country

indicators.note: outside says the first pieces stand round the next one

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
A is a commercial abbreviation for accepted, written on a bill

explanation.surface: Overseas money taken beyond the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West African' reads as one phrase, but 'West' gives W and the definition is 'African country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked nation in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Compulsion is part of procedures, sadly

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being forced to comply is a regrettable part of official routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure or threats that force someone to act.

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone queries an honest claim and judges it false and sneaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the quiet, secretly and by stealth, is acting surreptitiously.

indicators.note: containing says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: plates are layers, as in sheets of metal or rock strata
a fancy is a small iced cake

explanation.surface: Dishes holding elaborate sandwiches at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the sandwiches; it is a noun, a small decorated cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sandwich is a cake of tiers with a filling between them, so cakes in tiers are sandwiches.

parts.note: minor reads as small or lesser, but means a child under age who is brilliant

explanation.surface: A question about a second-rate brilliant mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who shows outstanding talent very early is a young prodigy, under age yet gifted.

parts.note: to form is to make
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Become friends in a properly ceremonious way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting officially and by the rules of etiquette is acting with ceremony.

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre company coped with staging a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera with spoken dialogue is a stage show set to music.

clue.text: Gross European average, nothing to us

parts.note: the norm is the average or standard
O is zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that European statistics are disgusting and irrelevant to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' suggests a financial figure such as gross domestic product; it means huge. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean very big or bulky, so it is a synonym for huge.

parts.note: Bt is the abbreviation for baronet, a hereditary British title
use is practice or custom, as in 'in common use'

explanation.surface: An aging titled gentleman's habit is slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slow to understand is dull and stupid.

definitions.meaning: a struggle is a hard try, an exertion
a piece of work produced, as in 'a fine first try'

explanation.surface: Battling to get a task finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort means both exertion and the attempt or achievement that results from it.

clue.text: Shock for fellow on Conservative wing

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top

parts.note: the right is the conservative wing of politics

explanation.surface: A scandal for a Tory member on the hard right.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden scare is a shock to the nerves.

clue.text: One politician given paintings to pass on

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament
art is paintings collectively

explanation.surface: A lone member of parliament is given artworks to hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to communicate or give, to hand on information.

indicators.note: reportedly signals what is said, so a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl

explanation.surface: Word is that a young woman is posing for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting pretty' looks like a girl posing, but it is the idiom for being well set up, as in 'you've got it made'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having it made means being comfortably successful, in a fortunate position.

clue.text: A chap entertaining a fellow from across the Atlantic

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding the guests inside

parts.note: a man is a chap
Eric is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man hosting another man who has come from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fellow from across the Atlantic' reads as one phrase, but 'a fellow' is wordplay and the definition is only 'from across the Atlantic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, someone from the USA is from across the ocean.

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: an ascent is a rise, progress upwards
the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside'. 'Youngster's' gives the definition plus 's, read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person, a youngster.

clue.text: Man would come round bearing notice

indicators.note: come round says the first words go around the next piece

parts.note: he'd is short for 'he would', a man would
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A man would turn up carrying a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice of something is to pay attention to it.
